chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated, saying: Some of our companions narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The master of this matter must have a disappearance, and he must have isolation during his disappearance. How good an abode is Tayba, and there is no loneliness among thirty!

key_terms.طَيْبَةٌ: Tayba (a name for Medina or a specific place)

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the Imam's disappearance and isolation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the occultation (ghaybah) and seclusion (izlah) as inevitable divine necessities for the Imam of the Age, ensuring his protection from enemies and the general public. The reference to 'Tayba' (the Good Land) signifies that despite the isolation, the Imam resides in a state of spiritual comfort and divine proximity, free from the psychological burden of loneliness (wahshah) that typically accompanies such seclusion.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (41) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from some of his companions from Ahmad bin Muhammad from al-Hasan bin Ali al-Washsha’ from Ali bin Abu Hamza from Abu Baseer that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said:
“The man of this matter must disappear and he is to be in isolation during his disappearance. How good abode Tayba is! No loneliness is among thirty!”
